output.name: Skelmi
output.myth:
Ennu sat on the cliff with a bone needle and a bolt of sailcloth, making a gull for a woman whose husband had gone to sea and not come back. He sewed the body and both wings, and he was on the last feather when the woman died under the smoke-hole. Ennu did not finish it. He tied off the thread and set it on the wind, and Tavo, who laughs at unfinished things, carried it past the Leeward Reach. Hesk counted the stitches as it went. A hundred and forty, she says, and one gap where the thread should have run.

The gull hangs in the Unflown, one wing open like a question. It looks east at Tikar, the Small Boot, where the sea kept a boot. North-west sits Halun, the Kite for the Drowned Child, with the child's name in its bridle knots. Sailors who see it say it will not come home, and that is no fault of the wind.

Grandmothers say to leave one loose stitch in every kite you make, so the thing you made has somewhere to go back to.
output.finding: Sailors far to the south find it by starting at Tikar, the Small Boot, and looking a little under one hand-span west, where a gull hangs with one wing open.
